newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola sees reaching EPS target in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola sees reaching EPS target in 1996.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co said Thursday it continues to expect its 1996 earnings per share will grow by the "upper teens to 20 percent" compared with the previous year.
"The company remains confident that it will meet its long-term objectives of upper teens to 20 percent growth in earnings per share in 1996," Coca-Cola spokesman Randy Donaldson said.
The Atlanta-based soft drink giant reported earnings of $1.18 a share in 1995 on a post stock split basis.

Donaldson's statement follows comments on November 20 by Chairman Roberto Goizueta that Coca-Cola's operating income in 1996 will be "give-or-take" $4 billion, 80 percent of which will be generated outside the United States.
Goizueta's comments were in reply to a question after a speech to the Executives Club here.
"Mr. Goizueta's comments yesterday at the Executives Club of Chicago were not in any way intended as a forecast of operating income for 1996," Donaldson said.

Donaldson added that Coca-Cola's operating income for the year have been impacted by the company's decision to reduce inventory. "Those decisions were offset by gains below the operating line," Donaldson added.
Coca-Cola shares were off 5/8 at 51, after reaching an intra-day low of 50-1/8.
